headline: Tonight's showers fade into a warm, dry stretch through Thanksgiving and Black Friday, while the bigger story is the coast: a Coastal Flood Watch for Wednesday–Thursday, when very high morning tides and a big west swell could bring significant flooding and damaging surf.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Sunday's cold front brought showers and a few thunderstorms, with 0.25–0.40 inch along the Central Coast and much less inland (0.05–0.15 inch). Showers continue Sunday night from the Channel Islands to the Ventura/Santa Barbara County line and along the Los Angeles County coast, moving east and dying off overnight, so Glendale and Burbank may catch a passing shower with brief gusty west winds through about 2 AM; there is a small chance of an isolated heavier shower, mostly near the coast, and about a 5 percent chance of thunder. A Frost Advisory runs until 8 AM Monday for the Antelope Valley and its eastern foothills, where lows drop near freezing, while clouds and fog should keep other inland areas a bit milder; Monday itself turns warm and dry.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: High pressure and light offshore (northeast) winds bring warm, dry weather Monday and Tuesday and start a warming trend that lasts through the week; the offshore winds stay weak and well below advisory levels. Highs reach the upper 60s to mid 70s across the coasts and coastal valleys by Tuesday and the upper 60s to 70s in many areas Wednesday. Another weak system brings light showers to northern San Luis Obispo County as early as Tuesday night, turning more showery with possible thunder Wednesday, with a quarter inch or less in San Luis Obispo and Santa Barbara counties; Los Angeles and Ventura counties have less than a 15 percent chance of measurable rain.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Thanksgiving Day and Black Friday look warm and dry under strong high pressure with weak northeast winds, and the chance of advisory-level winds is very low. Highs peak Friday in the 70s to lower 80s along the coast and in the coastal valleys and the mid 60s to lower 70s inland, about 4 to 8 degrees above normal. Another weak system crosses Saturday and Sunday, with timing still uncertain, bringing generally under a quarter inch of rain (up to 0.75 inch in far northwest San Luis Obispo County near Rocky Butte) and cooling highs back into the 60s to around 70.

coast: Forecasters have significant concern for moderate to major coastal flooding Thanksgiving week, from a combination of unusually high sea levels (warm ocean water expanding), extra-high tides with the moon at its closest, and a large long-period west swell. For the Central Coast, Ventura and Los Angeles counties, a Coastal Flood Advisory is in effect Monday–Tuesday (shallow flooding of beach parking lots and unprotected roads, moderate beach erosion), followed by a Coastal Flood Watch Wednesday–Thursday, when peak high tides between 8:45 and 10 AM reach about 8.2–8.4 feet for LA/Ventura and 7.9–8.2 feet for the Central Coast, with a reasonable worst case 0.3–0.5 foot higher; if upgraded to a warning, expect more extensive flooding farther inland and damage to coastal roads and structures. Areas of greatest concern include Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and Long Beach/Naples in LA County, Faria to Silver Strand Beach and Ventura Harbor in Ventura County, and Morro Bay, Pismo Beach, Oceano Dunes and the Cayucos, Avila and Pismo piers on the Central Coast; the Santa Barbara South Coast (Santa Barbara to Rincon, Jalama Beach) and Catalina and Santa Barbara islands have a Coastal Flood Advisory Monday–Thursday, and more hazards are likely needed Friday. A High Surf Advisory covers the Central Coast through Thursday afternoon, with surf up to 11 feet Monday morning, a lull Monday night into Tuesday, then rapid building to 10–15 feet Wednesday morning and 15–22 feet Wednesday afternoon and evening (likely upgraded to a High Surf Warning by Tuesday), plus breaking waves at the Morro Bay entrance Wednesday into possibly Thursday. LA and Ventura beaches get elevated to high surf all week, peaking Wednesday and Thursday with likely High Surf Advisories, a small chance of warning-level surf up to 15 feet on the Ventura coast, and breaking waves at the Ventura Harbor entrance Wednesday; stay off rock jetties and away from the water's edge. Offshore, winds and seas stay below small craft advisory levels through Tuesday night, then low-end advisory-level northwest to west winds are possible Wednesday and Wednesday night south of Point Conception as a 14–16 foot west swell brings large seas to the outer waters.
watch_for: Coastal Flood Watch Wednesday–Thursday: morning high tides plus a big west swell could bring moderate to major flooding at LA, Ventura and Central Coast beaches and harbors.
High surf peaking Wednesday–Thursday, up to 15–22 feet on the Central Coast and possibly 15 feet on the Ventura coast.
Frost in the Antelope Valley and its eastern foothills early Monday morning.
confidence: Forecasters see no major changes from earlier thinking and are confident in tonight's showers fading and a warm, dry week through Black Friday, with uncertainty mainly about how closely the swell and peak tides line up midweek and the timing of next weekend's weak system.
